newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY REWARDS ITS OLYMPIC CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY REWARDS ITS OLYMPIC CHAMPIONS.

text.p: Hungary on Wednesday passed a law rewarding its Olympic champions with a lifelong monthly payment equivalent to the national average salary, the Hungarian news agency MTI reported.

The law stipulates that resident Hungarians over the age of 36 who have gold medals from summer or winter Olympics, won either individually or in teams, will be entitled to an annuity from January 1 next year equal to the average salary for the previous year.
The widow or widower of an Olympic champion will be eligible for half the award, provided the couple lived together up the champion's death.
The payout in 1997 will cost the Hungarian state an estimated just over 50 million forints ($277,000).
Hungary has 139 Olympic champions. Sixteen of them are not yet 36 but will receive the annuity when they reach that age.
